task_context.problem_statement: $k, a_2, a_3$ and $k, b_2, b_3$ are both nonconstant geometric sequences with different common ratios.  We have  $$a_3-b_3=3(a_2-b_2).$$Find the sum of the common ratios of the two sequences.
task_context.reference_solution:
Let the common ratio of the first sequence be $p$ and the common ratio of the second sequence be $r$.  Then the equation becomes

$$kp^2-kr^2=3(kp-kr)$$
Dividing both sides by $k$ (since the sequences are nonconstant, no term can be $0$), we get

$$p^2-r^2=3(p-r)$$
The left side factors as $(p-r)(p+r)$.  Since $p\neq r$, we can divide by $p-r$ to get

$$p+r=\boxed{3}$$
